subject: Urgent: Medicore production error surge (5xx/429) — mitigation & exec check-in
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicore.io>
To: support@redwood.example, grace_oconnor@redwood.example
Cc: procurement@medicore.io
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Spike in 5xx/429 and timeouts — urgent

Hi Redwood team,

We started seeing a large increase in 5xx and 429 responses from your hosted inference API starting ~08:40 PDT after we released a batch of billing predictions. Our observability shows: p95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.8s, 5xx rate climbed from 0.2% to ~8% across our key endpoints, and we’re seeing many client-side timeouts. This is impacting user-facing flows.

Attached is a quick screenshot of our monitoring (prod_error_snapshot.png). We have an enterprise contract with an SLA and need immediate triage. Can someone confirm if this is a platform-wide issue or something specific to our Dedicated pool?

We’re available for a quick call now.

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Platform — Medicore Health
elena.morales@medicore.io
+1 415-555-0193

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicore.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 and timeouts — urgent

Elena — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. I’m opening an incident and escalating to SRE now. Initial questions while we triage:
- Are you on a Dedicated pool or hosted endpoint for these calls?
- Which model/version and sequence length are you hitting?
- Any recent traffic shaping or client-side retry changes?

Ben/Marissa/Markus — I’ve looped you in. Markus, can your team check GPU pool utilization and autoscaler logs for the Medicore namespace? If this is capacity exhaustion we’ll need an emergency scale/route.

Elena — we’ll aim to get an initial statement within 20–30 minutes and propose immediate mitigations. I’m available for a bridge now if you prefer.

— Grace
Grace O’Connor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.example

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Cc: ops@redwood.example
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 and timeouts — initial findings

Quick update from infra: we’re observing sustained GPU utilization at 98–100% across the Dedicated pool backing Medicore between 08:35–09:00 PDT. The autoscaler is healthy but is not adding capacity fast enough because: 1) many requests are holding GPU slots for long-running generation (higher sequence lengths) and 2) the request pattern caused retry amplification from client-side retries, which amplified queue pressure.

Top-level findings:
- Primary cause: pool capacity exhaustion leading to backend 5xx from OOM/queue-shed and 429s from our ingress throttler.
- Contributing factor: client retry loop (exponential retry) at Medicore that re-submitted timeouts into the system.
- Safe mitigations available now: temporarily enable emergency scale-up (hot-add GPUs) for the Dedicated pool, apply a short-lived routing rule to steer traffic to the fallback quantized model (reduced memory footprint), and implement a server-side early-429 backpressure window to break retry amplification.

Attached incident_timeline.csv contains the metric spike and node allocation timeline. I recommend we do:
1) Emergency scale-up (30min window)
2) Enable fallback routing for non-critical endpoints to quantized model v2-q8
3) Ask Medicore to reduce client-side retry aggressiveness (we can add short-lived 429 hints via header)

Taking these should reduce 5xx/429 in the next 10–20 minutes. I’ll stand by for approval to proceed.

-Markus
Markus Klein
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.example

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>
To: Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicore.io>
Cc: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike in 5xx/429 and timeouts — Redwood response and next steps

Elena — I’m Ben (your AE). Thank you for flagging this. Grace and Markus have outlined a mitigation path. We will:
- Stand up a short incident bridge for the next hour.
- Apply an emergency scale-up to your Dedicated pool and enable fallback routing to the quantized model for non-latency-critical calls.
- Share an incident timeline and follow-up RCA.

On the business side, I’ll coordinate with procurement if you need an SLA accommodation/credit while we stabilize. Marissa will be your CS point post-incident.

Can we schedule a 30-minute executive check-in tomorrow at 9am PT to review impact and credits?

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.example

From: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.example>
To: leadership@redwood.example, Elena Morales <elena.morales@medicore.io>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.example>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.example>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.example>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Medicore incident summary & ask — update and exec approval

Executive summary (for leadership + Medicore):
- Incident: sudden production surge causing GPU pool exhaustion and retry amplification, producing elevated 5xx/429 and p95 latency regressions for Medicore endpoints on 2026-10-20 08:35–09:15 PDT.
- Impact: customer-facing timeouts and degraded throughput; peak 5xx rate ~8%.
- Root cause (preliminary): Dedicated pool capacity hit due to larger-than-expected sequence lengths combined with aggressive client retries; autoscaling lagged because in-flight requests occupied resources.
- Mitigations applied (20 Oct): emergency hot-add capacity to Dedicated pool (+4 GPUs), enabled fallback routing to quantized model v2-q8 for non-critical routes, and configured short-lived ingress 429 backpressure to break retry amplification. Metrics normalized ~40 minutes after mitigations.
- Customer comms: Ben and I briefed Medicore; they’ve requested an exec call and potential SLA credit.

Asks for leadership:
1) Approve a temporary emergency capacity budget for the remedial scale-up charges (estimated $3,200 for the event window).
2) Approve offering Medicore a 30% service credit on their October invoice to cover user impact (Ben, please confirm if 30% aligns with our comp guidelines).

Attachments: mitigation_plan.txt (detailed steps executed), incident_timeline.csv, prod_error_snapshot.png

Next steps: Ben to coordinate credit/contract conversation; Marissa to lead postmortem with Medicore and collect client retry traces; Markus and infra to complete RCA and provide long-term autoscaler tuning recommendations.

Elena — would you like the exec call at 9am PT tomorrow? If that works we’ll get a calendar invite out.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O’Connor
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
grace_oconnor@redwood.example
